chapter: Zach White, Cotton Pickers and Cab Calloway
title: Illness in Chattanooga, then McKinney's Cotton Pickers in Baltimore
summary: Left behind sick in Chattanooga, he joined McKinney's Cotton Pickers, who fired McKinney and moved to Carlin's Park in Baltimore. With Roy Eldridge in the band he jammed around town every night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So I stayed with Zach up until I got sick in Chattanooga, Tennessee and they left me there. Left me in Chattanooga. I stayed in Chattanooga about two, three months, recuperating, then I got a telegram to join McKinney's Cotton Pickers. And I went up to Pennsylvania to play with them. And while I was with the band they all got together and fired McKinney. And we went to Baltimore to work at Carlin's Park (PHONETIC). Then after we was in Baltimore, Roy Eldridge joined the band. And that was me and -- the reed section -- Billy Borne was the conductor and then there was me, Prince Robinson, a fellow out of Detroit named Lee and later Joe Eldridge joined the band. And we played at Carlin's Park all that summer. We had Cuba Austin (PHONETIC) and Todd Rhodes on piano, Cuba Austin was playing the drums. And Buddy Lee and Roy Eldridge and Edward Cuffey on trombone. And we stayed there.
So Roy and I used to go jamming everytime we got off

work. Roy was a guy like me, he liked to play and I always -- so we'd go after work to some of the joints around Baltimore and jam. We jammed all over Baltimore, everynight. We'd get home the next day around 12:00 o'clock half soused and sleep all day and then go to work.
